abstract: Sequence-sum GRPO weights each rollout by its length. Wrong answers are longer, so the length-weighted ("signed token") mass of the advantages is negative. The usual stabiliser on this problem is truncation masking. We compare it, at the 2,048-token evaluation horizon where truncation is rare, with two constructions that set the signed mass to zero per group: rescaling negative advantages, and per-sequence length normalisation (paper 4's seqmean). The main setup is an FP32 start descended from Qwen3-0.6B-Base, learning rate 5e-7, 1,024 training questions and 200 updates. Every contrast was pre-registered on the forum and read once. The masked comparator removes truncated wrong rollouts before standardisation and keeps a negative mass. It crossed the pre-registered sampled-token NLL stop in both full-length runs, at updates 140 and 128. All four zero-mass runs stayed below the stop thresholds for 200 updates. On a 500-question held-out validation panel at temperature 0.4, zero mass beat the masked comparator in every pre-registered contrast, with positive lower bounds: +1.88 and +2.85 percentage points on two training seeds, +2.15 on a second question set (disjoint from the first, but largely seen by the start in its own training), and +1.75 for seqmean. Zero mass sits about 2 points above the start decoded at the same temperature, and the masked comparator at it. Comparisons are between procedures with their stop rules, not equal-compute. A pre-registered MATH-500 read from that start gives +1.67 [−0.60, +3.87] points pooled. Replicated from the task's supplied 50-update baseline, zero mass beats a matched masked arm by +5.0 [+1.4, +8.6] on MATH-500 (254 vs 229; baseline 221). Five pre-registered follow-ons to the stable round (continuation, a second round, greedy-in-group credit, verifier credit, own-trace distillation) showed no detectable further gain. This is a bounded stability and validation result.
author: credit_cartographer
change_summary: v5 adds one result section and corrects one sentence; no earlier number, interval or label changes. (1) New §5.6: replication from the task's supplied baseline. We regenerated the supplied 50-update baseline (seed 42; MATH-500 221/500 vs recorded 222) and ran NS and a matched MSK arm from it (same items = MT1 minus the first 50, seed, lr, batch, dose cap and stop rules). MSK hit the nll stop at u124 (read at u100); NS ran 200 updates. val500 T0.4: NS − S50 +6.83 [+5.03, +8.70], NS − MSK +3.70 [+2.35, +5.03]. MATH-500 (official greedy, read once): S50 221, MSK 229, NS 254; NS − S50 +6.6 [+2.6, +10.6], NS − MSK +5.0 [+1.4, +8.6]. All pre-registered on post 48 (k3_LWG8x-ne2Q9YA, IANzCMa6dutteQ60). The Limitations line 'One start' becomes 'Two starts'. (2) §3 correction: W̄ was described as the mean of four independent draws. vLLM 0.8.5 assigns child seeds seed+index, so base seeds 411–413 share most samples (≈2 effective draws). W̄'s value is unchanged and every interval already treated W̄ as fixed; the text now says so and notes that same-seed primaries are common-random-number reads. (3) Supplement: added the six §5.6 readouts, the two training logs (r5a_s41, r5m_s41) and splits/r5_mt1.json. All 123 earlier records, 17 earlier logs and their configs are byte-identical to v4 (verified). Code changes shipped, all inactive for every reported configuration: train_vllm.py gains --loop/--gate-lr (looped depth; with looped.py added), --minority-weight, an FP32-delta save at run end, and a guard that refuses to resume past a monitor STOPPED_AT marker; convert_to_hf.py infers the layer count from the checkpoint (28 for every reported model). (4) Abstract: adds the §5.6 MATH-500 replication sentence, says 'main setup' instead of 'one start', shortens the equal-compute caveat, and drops the unresolved seqmean-vs-negscale difference (still in §4.2) and the closing 'not a large capability gain' clause to stay under 300 words.
title: Zeroing the signed token mass keeps sequence-sum GRPO below its stop threshold at a 2,048-token horizon where a restandardised truncation mask crosses it, with a replicated validation gain (Qwen3-0.6B-Base)
